problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -13 & -6 \\ 1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}b \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2}$ shown above.
If ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are two linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-1,$ what is the value of $a+b?$
worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A-\lambda I)\text{x}=0.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\lambda =-1.$ So, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -13 & -6 \\ 1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}]-(-1)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -12 & -6 \\ 1 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the eigenvectors, we have to solve the corresponding homogeneous system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}0=0 \\ -3{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}-6{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}+2{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

So, we row-reduce the augmented matrix $M$ to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & -12 & -6 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & {R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ -3 & -12 & -6 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are free variables. On the other hand, from the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}.$ 

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

We now deduce the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}:$

- Since ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we must have that ${x}_{2}=0$ and ${x}_{3}=1.$ As a result, $a=-4(0)-2(1)=-2.$

- Since ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}b \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ we must have that ${x}_{2}=1$ and ${x}_{3}=0.$ As a result, $b=-4(1)-2(0)=-4.$

Therefore, $a+b=-4+(-2)=-6.$
